query: Does a .gitignore sitting in a subdirectory actually get honoured during the walk, and can a nested negation re-include a file its parent ignored?
How do markdown heading levels turn into a section's name, and what gets indexed for a doc that has no headings at all?
Why does a chunk repeat a function's docstring in a header line above the body when the body already contains it, and when is that line skipped?
Where does the file-level summary used for broad 'how does this codebase handle X' questions come from, and what happens if that LLM call fails mid-index?
Besides whole functions, is code indexed at a finer grain like individual if/for blocks or single statements, and are tiny ones skipped?
Does parsing need network access the first time it sees a new language, and how do I pre-download the grammars so indexing never touches the network?
In the Python parser, why is the synthetic module-docstring symbol appended before the AST walk instead of inserted at the front of the list afterwards?
When a function's body changes and its row is deleted and re-inserted on re-index, what stops other symbols' parent links and call edges from being silently nulled?
Why doesn't a ticket saying 'the test suite failed to run and update the process' get linked to functions actually named test, run, update or process?
In watch mode, what stops a debounce timer that fires at the exact moment it is cancelled from re-indexing the same file twice?
what happens to reranking if the cross-encoder library isn't installed?
when packing retrieved snippets into the final context, what keeps it from going over the token budget?
for each kind of question, what sets which search legs run and how deep the call-graph expansion goes?
why would we embed a made-up code snippet instead of the question the user actually typed?
what makes it search again after the model has already written an answer that sounds unsure?
how does it decide a search query is too short for embeddings to be worth running?
which retrieved symbols get their score multiplied for being important hubs, and where in the pipeline does that happen?
how can a function body that's too big for the remaining budget still be included instead of being dropped?
why does call-graph expansion skip the PageRank re-sort on repos with very few resolved call edges?
when the same chunk turns up in two different result lists, which one's source label is kept, and why isn't the higher score used to pick?
What tables does trelix create in its SQLite index, and how do files, symbols and chunks relate to each other?
Do we need a separate search engine for keyword search, or is BM25 ranking done inside SQLite itself?
I switched from a 3072-dimension cloud embedding model to a 384-dimension local one and search started returning garbage — how does trelix catch that?
How would we know if someone edited a row in the audit log after it was written?
When the store backend is set to qdrant instead of sqlite, which vector store gets used and how does the Qdrant collection get created on first run?
Where are the sparse SPLADE token weights persisted, and how is the dot-product score computed against them?
Several threads run keyword searches at once but they seem to serialize — can FTS5 reads be made to run in parallel?
What happens if the installed sqlite-vec version is too old to support an HNSW index — does indexing fail?
File-summary and sub-symbol vectors sit in the same table as normal chunk vectors — how do they avoid stealing slots from the top-k of an ordinary search?
Does the audit trail record the literal text of what users searched for, or is it redacted somehow?
how does the agent keep taking turns on its own until it has an answer, and what stops it looping forever?
when I set the LLM provider in my config, where does trelix turn that string into an actual chat client object, and why is each provider's SDK imported inside its own branch?
when a model API rate limits us, how long do we wait before trying again, and do we respect the delay the server asks for?
if the Bedrock model I configured is not enabled for on-demand use in my account, does the request just fail?
if I ask the same question twice, does it re-run the embedding model on my query text or reuse a cached vector?
does the wording of the answer change depending on what kind of question was asked, or is it one fixed prompt?
when reviewing a pull request, how does it figure out what surrounding code to pull in for a changed block before asking the model?
what keeps a markdown snippet that itself contains triple backticks from breaking out of the code block we wrap it in for the model?
why do some OpenAI model names get a different token-limit parameter than others when we call the chat API?
is the faithfulness number in the answer-quality evaluation a real semantic check, or just word overlap with the retrieved code?
does the HTTP server require an API key on every route, and what happens if I never set the auth token?
when I search all my registered repos at once, how does each repo's configured weight change the combined ordering, and how are duplicate hits dropped?
when an MCP client pages through search results with a cursor, is the underlying search re-run for each page?
if semgrep isn't installed or prints output we can't read, does taint analysis fail loudly or just come back empty?
can a caller authenticate with a JWT signed using HS256, or with no signature at all?
in the LangChain and LlamaIndex wrappers, does the k setting actually make retrieval cheaper or does it only trim the list afterwards?
where is the list of repositories used for cross-repo search kept on disk, and what happens if that file contains invalid JSON?
why does a code symbol that references a ticket end up with an edge in each direction in the code graph?
when I pipe trelix graph --json into jq, what stops the progress spinner from corrupting the JSON on stdout?
after a single file changes, does community detection re-run across the whole graph or only over part of it?
